My top candidates from the leaf class list: Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Late_Blight, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Early_Blight, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Verticillium_Wilt, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate (8 views total across 8 classes).

That's a microscope image, not useful for comparison. Let me check other candidates.

Bacterial Canker shows marginal leaf scorching/browning - different pattern from the test image. Let me check the remaining candidates.
Verticillium Wilt shows wilting with V-shaped yellowing - no bronzing or necrotic spots. Not a match. One more view remaining.

CMV shows mosaic mottling and leaf distortion without bronzing - not a match.

After viewing all 8 reference images across 8 classes, the comparison is clear:

| Candidate | Match? | Key difference |
|---|---|---|
| **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** | **Strong match** | Bronzing + scattered necrotic spots on upper leaf surface |
| Bacterial_Speck | No | Discrete spots on green leaves, no bronzing |
| Late_Blight | N/A | Microscope image |
| Septoria_Leaf_Blotch | No | Yellow leaf, not bronzed |
| Early_Blight | No | Large concentric-ring lesions |
| Bacterial_Canker | No | Marginal scorching pattern |
| Verticillium_Wilt | No | V-shaped yellowing, wilting |
| Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus | No | Mosaic mottling, distortion |

The test image shows **bronzing on upper leaf surfaces with numerous small dark necrotic spots and downward-cupping leaves**, which are the hallmark diagnostic features of TSWV. The TSWV reference image (Bugwood_10) was the only one that closely matched this distinctive bronzing + necrotic spot pattern.
